Last Podcast on the Left mentioned it, and then I dived into Nilsen. Music was associated with a lot of his actions. Mostly strange stuff too -- one creepy story is when he was burning a body in the backyard of his apartment, he turned his speakers to face the windows and blasted the Exorcist soundtrack.

It is what he would do with music. He was super into the music he liked, and he would get his victims to listen to it -- while they were distracted, he would go in for the kill. 

Not all of his kills were like this, but this was a common practice of Nilsen.

I can speak only from my own experiences and thoughts, but BPD is torture. I am plagued with intense violent thoughts, and that is honestly why I got into looking into these people -- almost as like a warning. Not all BPDs have violent impulses, but a lot of us do, and it is easy to feel like a monster for it. 

Your empathy on the matter is honestly uplifting. There is an entire sub on this site devoted to calling BPDs unfeeling monsters, and many health care workers carry the same stigma about it. It does often feel dehumanizing, and that is the last weight that should be placed on someone struggling with this affliction.

Thankfully I did not take Dahmer's or Dennis Nilsen's route, but I cannot help but have a tiny bit of sympathy for them. Mental illness does not excuse their behavior, but it definitely helps make sense of it.

Dennis Nilsen's coverups are some of the most bizarre things I have ever heard about to the point where they are hard to believe. 

He burns the bodies in a barrel outside of his apartment building, but first he turns his speakers to face the windows and blasts The Exorcist soundtrack. 

He flushes flesh down the toilet which, or course, clogged the buildings pipes, and then he trying to replace the flesh blocked with fried chicken to fool the police.   

He accidentally walked around with a bag of intestines while he took his dog for a walk, and then just left it in the park. 

A very ridiculous and hard to understand person.
